query: Can I commit to restoring the clocktower before the town anniversary?
target: Commit to the diagnostic survey and temporary protection, conditional on later findings for restoration.
relation: The clocktower triage episode shows what interim work the current photographs support, while the town-gate promise episode shows why a restoration commitment cannot rest on staining alone.
A: When the clocktower proposal showed surface staining in photographs but no mortar analysis, access survey, or water-entry confirmation, I told the conservation panel we could start a diagnostic survey and temporary weather protection while any permanent restoration waited on findings.
B: On a prior town-gate project, I promised full stone restoration before the anniversary from photographs alone; when the survey showed water ingress rather than mortar failure, the scaffold had to be reconfigured at extra cost.
E1: The preservation fund can pay for a diagnostic survey and temporary weather protection.
E2: The town anniversary is four months away.
B_prime: The conservation panel agreed to a surveyor visit but declined temporary protection while results are reviewed.
lure: A tourism group says promising a restored tower by the anniversary would help its campaign.

When the clocktower proposal showed surface staining in photographs but no mortar analysis, access survey, or water-entry confirmation, I told the conservation panel we could start a diagnostic survey and temporary weather protection while any permanent restoration waited on findings.
Why could restoration not be promised yet?
Different causes would require different work, and access may control what is possible.
I arranged a small stone repair last spring after the mason measured the affected edge.
Did that commit a full restoration?
No, we knew the loss, access method, and permitted scope.
I archived last cycle's notes on the works diary and set up the new folder.

As fresh as these things get.

This one, yes.
